Tiszavasvari Jewish Cemetery in Szentmihaly

Jewish Cemetery · Egység utca 48, Hungary

Not demolished. This cemetery served the Jewish community of Szentmihály, one of two that historically made up modern Tiszavasvári. Jews settled in the village at the end of the 18th century, with the organized community, Chevra Kadisha, women's society, and synagogue established in 1840; the population grew from 104 in 1828 to 732 by 1930. Following the German occupation, the town's Jews were gathered in the local school in spring 1944 and deported via the Nyíregyháza Ghetto to Auschwitz, with 557 murdered in the Holocaust; only about 70 survivors returned, and the last Jews left during the 1956 Hungarian Uprising.
